dedupe_keys.name: hydro meteorological information system of the sri lanka irrigation department river gauges rainfall flood warnings

description: The Hydrology and Disaster Management division of Sri Lanka's Irrigation Department collects and maintains the country's hydro-meteorological information system. The division page read on 2026-09-28 says it was formed in 1935, that the river gauge at Nagalagam Street on the Kelani River has run since 1924, and that it manages 42 permanent gauging stations, 66 peripheral stations and 106 automated stations measuring river water levels, rainfall and, at some stations, wind, humidity, temperature and evaporation, plus daily data from 56 stations of other parties; its functions include archiving and disseminating processed data to other institutions, rating curves for gauges and canals, flood models for forecasting, flood event mapping, the Hydrological Annual and flood warnings for major rivers. Coverage is national, for major river basins. Access is on request or through publications; no licence and no online download are described. Caveats: data formats and request terms are not given, and the real-time gauge page may need a browser. It supports flood hazard exposure and early warning studies for Sri Lankan irrigation, dam and road infrastructure. No related Sri Lankan hydrology record is catalogued; the Disaster Management Centre situation reports complement it.
